note: Small rustic first-come, first-served Forest Service campground along the West Fork Methow River near Mazama, ~9 mi up Lost River Rd + gravel FR 5400; ~7 sites including a pull-through fitting RVs to 35 ft, vault toilet, no potable water. On-site Scan-and-Pay via rec.gov. --Claude

Colville NF campground on Swan Lake, ~14 mi SW of Republic via WA-21 and paved FR 53 (Scatter Creek). 26 sites (incl 4 walk-in tent sites) in a mixed-pine setting; the lakeshore loop accommodates moderate-size trailers/RVs with lake views and the non-lakeshore loop holds the pull-through sites. Potable water, vault toilets, no hookups. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay). --Claude

Colville NF campground on Crawfish Lake in the Okanogan Highlands, reached via Tunk Valley Rd/County Rd 9320 (~18.5 mi) and FR 3000-100 from Riverside. 19 sites (15 single, 4 double), 11 bordering the lakeshore; picnic table and fire ring each, boat launch (electric motors only), no potable water or garbage. Max trailer ~24 ft (not all sites fit that). First-come, first-served. --Claude

Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Tonasket RD) campground on North Fork Salmon Creek, ~2 mi north of Conconully via County Rd 2361/FR 38. Two loops, 12 sites (11 single, 1 double); picnic table, fire ring, vault toilets; no potable water, no hookups, no dump. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay), open ~May 1-Oct 27. --Claude

Colville NF (Republic RD) campground on the NE shore of Long Lake; 12 sites with picnic tables/fire pits, vault toilets, hand-pump potable water, boat launch. First-come, first-served. Accommodates tents up to larger RVs, but larger rigs should use caution on the narrow, rough entrance road (FR 5300-400). Non-motorized fly-fishing lake. --Claude

Colville NF (Three Rivers RD) campground along Sherman Creek off WA-20 west of Kettle Falls; 12 primitive sites on one loop, vault toilets, no potable water, ~1 mi paved accessible trail. RVs up to 30 ft. First-come, first-served. Open ~Memorial Day-Labor Day. --Claude

Small concessionaire-managed Colville NF campground on Lake Leo in the Little Pend Oreille chain of lakes; ~8 sites, vault toilets, drinking water, shallow boat launch, some sites with lake views. Open ~Memorial Day-Labor Day. --Claude

Colville NF campground on the east shore of Gillette Lake (Little Pend Oreille chain of lakes); 14 sites with paved interior roads/spurs, bear boxes, no hookups or dump, boat launch, swimming, fishing. Reservable online. --Claude

Colville NF campground on Pierre Lake; 15 sites in two areas (6 north-end sites for smaller rigs, 9 south-end sites with a tight J-hook turnaround best for truck campers/tents). North-end sites best for rigs to ~23 ft. Vault toilets, potable water, boat ramp and 175-ft fishing dock; no hookups. First-come, first-served. --Claude

Colville NF campground at Sherman Pass on WA-20 (Sherman Pass Scenic Byway), elev ~5,200 ft. 9 tent/trailer sites; a firsthand review parked a 23-ft rig in site 6, with sites suitable for RVs to ~35 ft. Potable water, vault toilets, tables/fire pits; pack-it-in/out (no trash), no hookups. First-come, first-served. --Claude

Colville NF (Newport/Sullivan Lake RD) campground on 32-acre South Skookum Lake near Usk; 24 sites in two loops (inner-loop parking aprons for smaller rigs; outer-loop walk-in tent sites with lake views). Larger sites fit rigs to ~31 ft (some sites 22 ft) so a 23-ft rig fits the larger sites. Vault toilets, drinking water, bear boxes; no hookups. First-come, first-served. Access via Kings Lake Rd (county) + 0.5 mi forest road. --Claude

Colville NF campground on high-elevation Browns Lake (fly-fishing only, no motorized boats); 18 drive-in sites, RVs to ~22 ft, vault toilets, no drinking water, lakeside access. First-come, first-served. --Claude

Colville NF campground on 75-acre Lake Ellen; the East loop has 11 drive-in sites with parking spurs (RVs to ~22 ft), vault toilet, no drinking water, single-lane gravel loop. First-come, first-served. --Claude

note: BLM (Spokane District) recreation site on Coffeepot Lake in the channeled scablands SW of Harrington; 7 first-come first-served drive-in sites with picnic table and fire ring, vault toilet, graveled boat launch and fishing dock, no potable water (pack it in/out). Access road is steep gravel - about 5 sites fit smaller trailers/truck campers to ~23 ft; not recommended for large rigs. --Claude

Whitman County fairgrounds 5 mi west of Colfax; the county permits camping year-round, not just during the fair. Grassed sites with water + electric, RVs to 50 ft, dump station, restrooms/showers plus pit toilets; RV self-serve check-in, no reservations (first-come, first-served). County-operated (pef@co.whitman.wa.us). --Claude

Jefferson County Parks & Rec campground on US 101 in Quilcene, next to the community center. 9 wooded sites (picnic table + fire ring), toilet, fresh water; RVs to ~30 ft. First-come, first-served, open ~Apr 1-Oct 31. --Claude

Okanogan County fairgrounds RV park at 175 Rodeo Trail Rd, operating as a public RV campground (open year-round except the county-fair closure, ~late Aug-mid Sep). 64 full-hookup sites, 44 electric/water sites, plus dry/tent camping; showers, restrooms, Wi-Fi. Reservable online (Firefly), FCFS otherwise. --Claude

Pend Oreille County fairgrounds in Cusick, inside a bend of the Pend Oreille River, operating as a public campground open to overnighters (up to a 2-week stay; closed to non-participants only during county-fair week). Sites with power & water, showers, restrooms. No on-site dump (nearest at Kalispel RV Park ~1/4 mi north). Notify caretaker 24 hrs ahead. --Claude

In-town paved RV park in east Vancouver next to Vancouver Mall, a handy base for visiting Portland; full hookups 20/30/50-amp, laundry, bathhouses, dog park; short- and long-term sites. Reservable. --Claude

Small in-town RV park at 802 N Morton St in Colfax (Palouse region, near Pullman/WSU). 9 gravel full-hookup sites (30/50-amp, water/sewer/cable), free EV charging; accepts nightly transient guests as well as weekly/monthly; often full, call ahead. --Claude

In-town Forks RV park across US-101 from Forks Outfitters/Thriftway; basecamp for Olympic NP (Hoh Rainforest, coast). ~33-42 full-hookup sites (20/30/50-amp), grass pull-throughs, big-rig friendly; clean restrooms, hot showers, coin laundry, WiFi; family-friendly, year-round. --Claude

Resort on the south shore of Lake Quinault (516 S Shore Rd) in the Quinault Rain Forest. 31 back-in RV sites with water + 30-amp electric (no sewer/dump on site); on-site restaurant and store, coin showers; open year-round (restrooms closed in winter); adjacent to the World's Largest Spruce. --Claude

Olympic National Forest campground off Forest Rd 24 (SR-119) near Lake Cushman and the Staircase entrance; forested drive-in loop sites in second-growth timber, no hookups, potable water, RVs to 36 ft. First-come, first-served (no reservations); cashless. --Claude

Lutheran-affiliated camp/retreat center ~7 mi E of North Bend on SE Middle Fork Rd; open to families and individuals as well as groups. Offers standard RV sites with utilities ($300/week) plus dry RV camping (may not be level) in a forest meadow; drive-in gravel/paved access. --Claude

Transient RV park with par-3 and mini golf just N of I-90 at Ephrata; full-hookup pull-through sites (20/30/50 amp W/E/S, cable) to 65 ft plus grass tent sites; pool, on-site stocked fishing ponds, laundry, WiFi. --Claude

Small family-owned transient RV park in the town of Wilbur off US-2, ~20 mi S of Grand Coulee Dam; 37 full-hookup (20/30/50 amp) sites plus a few power-only and dry/tent sites; laundry, showers, on-site cafe. --Claude

USFS campground in Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Methow Valley RD), ~18 mi west of Winthrop off Hwy 20 then 1.3 mi on FR 300 (maintained gravel spur); 46 forested sites, RVs to 34 ft (fits a 23-ft rig; many sites unlevel, arrive early), vault toilets and hand-pump water. First-come, first-served. Near Early Winters Creek. --Claude

Large campground on the west shore of Baker Lake maintained by Puget Sound Energy (utility operator), ~8 mi north of Concrete just south of Baker Dam off SR 20; ~108 tent/RV drive-in sites, main loop has water and sewer hookups, overflow loop is dry camping; first-come, first-served (free dry camping off-season). Boat launches nearby. --Claude

Small in-town RV park at 7 N Western Ave, Tonasket, operated by the Tonasket Chamber of Commerce (adjacent to City Hall/Visitor Center, near the Okanogan River). Full hookups incl water/sewer/50-amp, dump station, big-rig friendly (up to 50 ft), open year-round with a discounted extended-stay option. Reserve/inquire by phone. --Claude

Campground operated by Seattle City Light (city municipal utility) at Boundary Dam/Reservoir on the Pend Oreille River, NE corner of WA. 22 sites (3 ADA), roughly 12 that fit RVs (Class C-size), no hookups; flush toilets, potable water, trash, boat launch and dock, day-use area. First-come, first-served, 6-day max stay. --Claude

Colville National Forest (Sullivan Lake RD) campground on the east bank of the Pend Oreille River, ~2 mi N of the Ione bridge on Box Canyon Rd. 20 sites (001-020), no hookups; gravel/grass spurs said to fit any size RV. Vault toilets, drinking water, on-site boat ramp, camp host. Reservable on recreation.gov, open ~late May-early Sept. --Claude

Oregon Dept. of Forestry campground in the Tillamook State Forest along Gales Creek off OR-8/OR-6. ~23 primitive sites, no hookups, vault toilets and hand-pump water; many sites fit small RVs/trailers (rigs over ~25 ft have trouble, so a 23-ft rig fits some sites). First-come, first-served, no reservations; self-pay, open May-Oct. --Claude

Small Malheur National Forest (USFS, Blue Mountain Ranger District) forest camp along Camp Creek on a maintained forest road southwest of Prairie City. 6 sites incl pull-throughs (USFS lists RVs to ~37 ft), vault toilet, no potable water; first-come, first-served. --Claude

flag: 'Free with ODFW parking/day-use permit' left untouched: permit-based camping text (ODFW wildlife area parking permit)

note: USFS Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Powers RD). 14 forested sites strung along the South Fork Coquille River, ~15 mi south of Powers on FR33; paved drive-in access fitting RVs to ~30 ft, vault toilets, drinking water (Memorial Day-Labor Day), no hookups. Cashless via recreation.gov Scan & Pay (eff. July 2026). --Claude

USFS Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Powers RD). Small 7-site campground on Rock Creek (a South Fork Coquille tributary), ~18 mi south of Powers via FR33 then 1 mi on FR3347; vault toilet, no drinking water. RVs over 35 ft not recommended (smaller rigs fit). Cashless via recreation.gov Scan & Pay (eff. July 2026). --Claude

Small USFS campground (Rogue River-Siskiyou NF, High Cascades RD) near the confluence of Beaver Dam and Daley Creeks off Dead Indian Memorial Hwy / FR 37. 6 sites (3 tent, 3 designated trailer sites), vault toilet, no potable water, pack-out trash; drive-in on maintained gravel forest road. First-come, first-served, open ~June-Oct. --Claude

BLM campground in the Hyatt Lake Recreation Area east of Ashland, on the west side of Hyatt Reservoir. 12 sites in an open setting, well hand-pump water, vault toilets, undeveloped boat launch; accommodates RVs and tents. Reservable on recreation.gov, open ~late May-Oct 1. --Claude

USFS campground (Wallowa-Whitman NF) on the south shore of Phillips Reservoir in open ponderosa pine, off Hudspeth Lane / FR 2220. 11 tent/trailer sites plus 4 tent-only, vault toilets, no potable water; managed by the Anthony Lakes Campgrounds concessionaire, open ~May-Sept. --Claude

USFS campground (Wallowa-Whitman NF, Unity RD) along the South Fork of the Burnt River, ~7.5 mi west of Unity on FR 6005. 12 tent/trailer sites plus 2 tent-only, reconstructed 2008 with pull-through trailer parking under pine/fir; popular for fishing and Blue Mountain OHV trails. Reservable on recreation.gov, open ~May-Nov; elev ~4,400 ft. --Claude

Deschutes NF (Bend-Fort Rock RD) FCFS camping area at the historic 1920s-30s Fort Rock Ranger Station site in open ponderosa/grassland, reached via graveled Cabin Lake Rd (FS 18). Rustic, open sites accommodate RVs to ~30 ft; no potable water, vault toilet, open year-round. Known for bird-viewing blinds. First-come, first-served. --Claude

Deschutes NF (Bend-Fort Rock RD) campground on the summit of Pine Mountain by Pine Mountain Observatory, ~34 mi SE of Bend. 6 primitive sites, First-come, first-served. Vault toilets, no potable water. Gravel access road; small trailers fine, larger rigs need a careful driver on tight turns. --Claude

Dispersed camping on an open gravel bar along the Wild and Scenic Chetco River, ~3 mi up FR 1376 (North Bank Chetco River Rd) from the forest boundary in Rogue River-Siskiyou NF. Wide open gravel bar fits larger rigs; primitive, no hookups or water. Cashless Scan & Pay via recreation.gov, FCFS. Winter gravel-bar camping discouraged due to frequent high-water events. --Claude

Dispersed camping on an open gravel bar along the Wild and Scenic Chetco River, ~6 mi up FR 1376 (North Bank Chetco River Rd), just past Little Redwood CG, in Rogue River-Siskiyou NF. Long open gravel bar fits larger rigs; primitive, no hookups or water. FCFS. Winter gravel-bar camping discouraged (high-water events). --Claude

Malheur National Forest campground off Forest Road 17 (via FR 054) between Burns and John Day. About 12 sites in ponderosa pine with compressed-gravel pads, raised fire rings, picnic tables, and a vault toilet; no potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served. Suitable for smaller RVs. --Claude

USFS Malheur NF (Blue Mountain RD), on US-395 ~16 mi south of John Day at ~5,150 ft in ponderosa pine. Two loops (~11-15 sites), upper loop mostly pull-throughs plus back-ins; vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served (all Malheur NF camping is FCFS). No published RV length limit; pull-through sites fit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

USFS Umpqua NF (Tiller RD) on the upper South Umpqua River among old-growth cedar/fir. 5 standard sites, max vehicle length 22 ft, no restrooms or potable water, first-come, first-served. NOTE: currently closed for danger-tree treatment (no reopening date posted) -- verify status before visiting. --Claude

USFS Umpqua NF (Tiller RD) along Jackson Creek (South Umpqua tributary) on Forest Road 29, ~13 mi up Jackson Creek Rd. 7 primitive sites, max vehicle length 22 ft, no potable water, on-site fee tubes, first-come, first-served. NOTE: currently closed for danger-tree treatment (no reopening date posted) -- verify status before visiting. --Claude

BLM Northwest Oregon District, Nestucca River Recreation Area, along the Nestucca River in the Coast Range. 11 standard sites + a group shelter, each with picnic table, fire ring and paved parking; 2 vault toilets, well water (potable, may be off in low season). Reservable online or pay-on-arrival via the rec.gov app (no cell service). Season ~May-Sep; tent and small/mid RV. --Claude

USFS dispersed camping along Forest Rd 70 W of Chemult (Fremont-Winema NF). No facilities; large level pull-offs in lodgepole forest at a crossroads ~1 mi in. Gravel road in good shape but heavily washboarded; reviews confirm it accommodates 24-ft Class C rigs. First-come, first-served. --Claude

USFS Fremont-Winema NF, along the Williamson River just off US-97 ~5 min N of Chiloquin. 19 sites (some pull-through), picnic table/fire grate, vault toilets, hand pumps; no hookups. Most sites take RVs to 30 ft; first-come, first-served. Popular trout fishing on the Williamson. --Claude

Deschutes NF (Crescent RD) primitive campground on the SE edge of the district bordering Gilchrist State Forest, ~7 sites in lodgepole/ponderosa with a pit toilet. Popular with ATV/OHV riders and hunters. First-come, first-served. Access ~6 mi on gravel FR 9768 off Hwy 97 (drive-in). --Claude

Deschutes NF (Crescent Ranger District) on the east shore of Davis Lake below a large lava flow; 6 primitive sites for RV/trailer/tent, no drinking water, vault toilet, first-come, first-served. Max vehicle length 36 ft. Access road to the NE shore is closed in spring/early summer to protect wildlife. --Claude

Ochoco NF campground near the headwaters of Frazier Creek in ponderosa pine; 10 sites with varied-length spurs, some fitting RVs up to 40 ft, vault toilet, no potable water. Northern gateway to the Winom-Frazier OHV trail system. First-come, first-served. --Claude

Umpqua NF (Cottage Grove Ranger District) campground beside Brice Creek, 10 sites, RVs pull into all sites (a couple pull-through), no hookups/dump, vault toilets, no potable water. Reservable online. --Claude

Rustic Wallowa-Whitman NF (Hells Canyon NRA) campground in open pine/grassland near Billy Meadows: 12 sites (4 tent/trailer, 8 tent-only), vault toilet, no water, no hookups. Reached via ~40 mi of maintained gravel forest roads (FR 46) off Hwy 3 north of Enterprise. First-come, first-served, self-pay; season ~June-early Oct. --Claude

Primitive 5-site Wallowa-Whitman NF camp along the Wild & Scenic Lostine River (~5,200 ft), picnic table + fire ring, vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups. Accessed via Lostine River Road/FR 8210 (paved then rough, narrow, washboard gravel) - passable by smaller rigs (horse trailers use it) but tight for big RVs. First-come, first-served, self-pay; season ~June-Sept. --Claude

Mt. Hood NF campground on the Wild & Scenic Clackamas River off Hwy 224 east of Estacada: 11-12 sites, RVs to ~26 ft (interior roads tight for larger rigs), vault toilet, drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served; open ~April-Oct. Riverside Fire (2020) damage - watch for hazard trees. --Claude

Mt. Hood NF campground on the Wild & Scenic Clackamas River off Hwy 224 east of Estacada: 15 sites for tents or RVs to ~28 ft, vault toilet, no hookups. First-come, first-served; in 2026 opens only once nearby Lockaby CG fills. Riverside Fire (2020) recovery ongoing. --Claude

Mt. Hood NF campground on the south shore of Timothy Lake beneath Mt. Hood: ~43 single-family sites for tents/trailers/RVs to ~35 ft, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Fully reservable online; season ~late May-Sept. --Claude

USFS (Mt. Hood NF, Clackamas River Ranger District). Small (~10-site) drive-in campground on the Wild & Scenic Clackamas River near its confluence with the Collawash, ~1,600 ft; 2026 season 5/23-9/30, no hookups, tent/RV sites. Max RV length not posted. First-come, first-served. --Claude

Primitive BLM camping at Willow Creek (Whitehorse) Hot Springs, remote SE Oregon near Fields/Steens, ~4,525 ft; ~6 undesignated sites, one vault toilet, no potable water. Access is well-graded gravel from Fields, then dirt; the last ~2.5 mi is rough (potholes/mud) but passable by most vehicles and RVs; firsthand review reports a 30-ft trailer fitting a site. First-come, first-served. --Claude

USFS (Mt. Hood NF, Clackamas River Ranger District). Small drive-in campground on the Wild & Scenic Clackamas River just upstream of Carter Bridge; heavily burned in the 2020 Riverside Fire but operating first-come, first-served in 2026. Max RV length not posted; drive-in tent/RV sites. First-come, first-served. RV Life unrated (0*)/$ (auto 7/2026). --Claude

USFS (Mt. Hood NF, Clackamas River Ranger District). Small (~13-site) drive-in campground along the Oak Grove Fork of the Clackamas River near the historic Ripplebrook junction; operating first-come, first-served in 2026, no hookups, tent/RV sites. Max RV length not posted. First-come, first-served. RV Life unrated (0*)/$ (auto 7/2026). --Claude

BLM (Prineville District) campground at the end of the Lower Deschutes River Access Road, on the east bank of the lower Deschutes. 18 individual + 2 group sites, vault toilets, no water or hookups; big rigs fit but the gravel access road is washboard (drive ~20 mph). First-come, first-served, open year-round. --Claude

Wallowa-Whitman NF campground beside Fish Lake in the Wallowa Mountains (~6,700 ft), reached by a long forest road. 21 tent/trailer sites; 6 upper-loop sites accommodate RVs over 20 ft and 6 are accessible; potable water. Reservable online. Watch mosquitoes and late-summer drawdown. --Claude

Wallowa-Whitman NF (Pine RD) campground along North Pine/Lake Fork Creek on the paved Hells Canyon Scenic Byway (FR 39), ~8 mi off OR-86 near Halfway. ~10-11 forested sites, hand-pump water, vault toilets, no hookups; first-come, first-served. Sites are small and shaded -- larger rigs should scout. Open ~late May through late Oct. --Claude

Malheur NF (Emigrant Creek RD) campground on the shore of Yellowjacket Lake; ~20 open drive-in sites fitting trailers/RVs, vault toilets, hand-pump drinking water (seasonal). First-come, first-served. Reached by ~33 mi of paved/gravel forest roads from Burns. The surrounding forest burned in the 2024-25 Falls Fire and the campground was closed through 2025; the closure order expired at the end of 2025 (loop and lake intact on satellite) — verify open before a trip. Elev ~4840 ft. --Claude Rechecked 2026-09-30: closed under the Falls Fire area closure (recreation.gov). --Claude

Umatilla NF (Heppner RD) FCFS campground atop Coalmine Hill; one larger pull-in site near the entrance plus sites around a large parking area big enough to turn an RV or horse trailer, one vault toilet, a horse corral, and trailhead access to the Willow Creek/Bald Mountain/Hells Half Acre trails; no potable water or garbage service. First-come, first-served. Maintained Memorial Day to mid-November; ~22 mi from Heppner on County Road 678. Elev ~4850 ft. --Claude

Small Wallowa-Whitman NF (La Grande RD) campground in open ponderosa pine near a meadow, 12.5 mi NW of La Grande via I-84 exit 248 then FR 21 (1.5 mi). 4 single sites, each with table/fire ring/gravel parking area; no potable water, no hookups. Self-pay, reservable on recreation.gov. Open May-Oct. Open-pine layout with parking pull-ins fits a 23-ft rig. --Claude

Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area (USFS) campground off I-84 exit 51 near Cascade Locks, set in Douglas-fir/bigleaf-maple forest along Gorton Creek. 13 single sites + 3 group sites; RVs/trailers under 30 ft. Potable water, flush toilet, no hookups. Sites 1-2 FCFS, rest reservable on recreation.gov. --Claude

Small rustic Wallowa-Whitman NF campground (~5 sites, ~5,260 ft) on the Zumwalt Prairie rim near Buckhorn Overlook; open ponderosa/grassland. Reached by ~40 mi of gravel Zumwalt/Forest Rd 46, graded and passable by passenger vehicles when dry (not maintained off-season). Vault toilet, no water, FCFS, June–Sept. --Claude

Wallowa-Whitman NF campground in old-growth ponderosa along the Wild & Scenic Imnaha River, off FR 39 (Wallowa Mountain Loop Rd, paved); 13 drive-in sites with tables/fire rings/parking, well water, vault toilets, primary season June–Sept. --Claude

USFS Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Siskiyou Mtns RD) day-use/camp area on the east shore of Applegate Lake, ~0.5 mi below the dam. 7 tent sites plus 8 lakeside dry RV pull-ins (no hookups); rec.gov RV1 lists max RV/trailer 40 ft on a paved back-in, so a 23-ft rig fits easily. Groomed lawn slopes to the lake; store, boat ramp, fish-cleaning station. Reservable online, early May-mid Sept. --Claude

BLM (Vale District) primitive campground in the Leslie Gulch Area of Critical Environmental Concern, in a side canyon along Slocum Creek near the mouth at Lake Owyhee. 9 designated sites with picnic tables, sun shelters and fire pits; no water, vault toilets, 14-day limit. First-come, first-served. ~24 mi of maintained gravel (Leslie Gulch Rd) -- passable by a normal vehicle when dry (high-clearance advised if wet); BLM says large RVs not recommended but a 23-ft rig can reach the defined pull-in sites in dry conditions. --Claude

USFS Wallowa-Whitman NF (Wallowa Mountains Office) camp at the end of Forest Rd 3960 on the Wild & Scenic Imnaha River, gateway to the Eagle Cap Wilderness/Hells Canyon NRA. 10 single-family sites (tent/RV/equestrian sections), picnic table + fire ring, no hookups; reservable online, use season roughly June-Sept. Reached by ~9 mi of maintained gravel forest road. --Claude

BLM (Vale District) recreation site on the North Fork Malheur River, ~6 mi north of Juntura on maintained gravel Beulah Reservoir Rd. ~19-30 sites in a cottonwood riparian corridor, picnic tables + fire rings/grills, potable water (May-Oct), vault toilets, no hookups; first-come, first-served. RV length limit ~28 ft. --Claude

Small USFS Fremont-Winema NF camp on Odessa Creek at the west edge of Upper Klamath Lake, off Hwy 140 via FR 3639 (~22 mi W of Klamath Falls). 6 sites (listed to 35 ft but rough access road and tight spacing favor shorter rigs; a 23-ft rig fits), picnic tables/fire rings, one vault toilet, no potable water, small-boat ramp; first-come, first-served, open ~mid-May to mid-Dec. --Claude

USFS Wallowa-Whitman NF (La Grande RD) camp on the banks of the Grande Ronde River, ~5 mi south of Hwy 244 on FR 51. 12 tent/trailer sites (spurs ~33-45 ft, incl 3 double/group), paved roads, accessible vault toilets, no potable water; first-come, first-served via self-pay. --Claude

Small primitive Fremont-Winema NF (Lakeview RD) forest camp NE of Lakeview in a ponderosa-pine stand beside a spring-fed creek; 3 sites with picnic tables and fire rings, vault toilet, no potable water or hookups; drive-in via gravel FS roads 3615/3720; first-come, first-served. RV Life tags it dnr but it is USFS-managed (federal). --Claude

Fremont-Winema NF (Bly RD) campground on Dog Lake W of Lakeview; ~20-26 sites across several loops with picnic tables, fire rings, four vault toilets and two pavilion shelters for trailers/RVs, boat ramp and fishing dock, no potable water/trash (pack it out), no hookups; non-motorized/electric-motor boating. First-come, first-served. FS-managed (federal), not BLM. --Claude

Small FCFS Fremont-Winema NF forest camp on Drews Creek off Dog Lake Rd, ~35 min SW of Lakeview; about 5 drive-in sites (space for 4-5 small RVs plus tents), picnic tables/fire rings, vault toilets, no potable water. Gravel access. First-come, first-served. --Claude

FCFS Fremont-Winema NF campground on the Wild & Scenic North Fork Sprague River, SW of Paisley; 7 drive-in sites for tents/RVs/trailers, picnic tables/fire grates, vault toilet, potable water, open ~May 15-Oct 15. Area burned in the 2021 Bootleg Fire but the campground reopened. First-come, first-served. --Claude

Small FCFS Fremont-Winema NF forest camp (Lakeview RD, E side of the Warner Mtns) ~35 min NE of Lakeview; 7 spacious back-in drive-in sites among ponderosa/lodgepole/aspen, picnic tables/fire grates, vault toilet, hand-pump potable water, gravel FS 3615 access, open ~May 15-Oct 15. First-come, first-served. --Claude

Small FCFS Fremont-Winema NF forest camp (Lakeview RD, Warner Mtns) at ~6,480 ft SE of Lakeview; 3 drive-in sites among ponderosa/white fir/aspen by the spring, picnic tables/fire grates, vault toilet, no potable water. Gravel FS-road access. First-come, first-served. --Claude

Small FCFS Fremont-Winema NF forest camp (Lakeview RD, Warner Mtns) at ~6,073 ft along Willow Creek; 8 drive-in sites among ponderosa/aspen, picnic tables/fire grates, vault toilet, no potable water, open ~May 15-Oct 15. Gravel FS-road access. First-come, first-served. --Claude

BLM Prineville District campground on the Lower Deschutes Wild & Scenic River near Gateway/Madras. 21 individual sites plus 3 group-use sites, no hookups, vault toilets, no potable water; parking spurs 24-100 ft with some pull-throughs (fits a 23-ft rig). First-come, first-served (pay kiosk/fee box); open year-round. Access is gravel with a 14-ft-high tunnel near the entrance (height, not length, limit). --Claude

BLM Roseburg District, on the Umpqua River off Bullock Rd. 15 sites in two areas (5 north, 10 south); paved access roads, drinking-water spigots, vault toilets, no hookups; RVs to ~80 ft per rec.gov. Reservation-only via recreation.gov. River/boat access, popular with anglers. --Claude

USFS Ochoco NF (Paulina RD) campground straddling Sugar Creek in a ponderosa pine flat off a paved FS road ~13 mi NE of Paulina. Sites vary in size; many accommodate moderate-sized RVs, no hookups, no potable water. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

Primitive campground in Hart Mountain National Antelope Refuge (USFWS), ~4 mi south of refuge HQ near the Antelope hot springs. ~25-30 spread-out sites for tents and trailers up to 24 ft, vault toilets, fire rings, no water/hookups. No reservations, 14-day limit, open year-round; reached on maintained gravel roads (Hart Mountain/Hot Springs Rd) passable by most vehicles. --Claude

BLM Lakeview District free public rockhounding area (dispersed camping, no designated sites) in the Rabbit Basin ~20+ mi N of Plush. Facilities are a pit toilet, picnic tables and a shade structure; camp anywhere in the collection area. Main area reached on graded gravel (Hogback Rd/CR 3-10 then BLM roads); high-clearance recommended for the rough interior 2-tracks to prime digging spots. First-come, first-served, no hookups/water. --Claude

Ochoco NF campground at ~5,000 ft on a single loop near 170-acre Antelope Flat Reservoir, ~40 mi SE of Prineville via Hwy 380/FR 17. 23 sites incl pull-through RV spaces, no hookups, hand-pump potable water, vault toilet; boat ramp and day-use at the water's edge. First-come, first-served, mid-May to mid-Oct. Sites are a short walk back from the water. --Claude
Small 5-site Malheur NF (Blue Mountain RD) campground on the Middle Fork John Day River off Co Rd 20; vault toilet, no potable water. One site fits a ~30-ft rig. First-come, first-served. --Claude

9-site Malheur NF (Blue Mountain RD) campground near Dixie Summit off Hwy 26, close to the Sumpter Valley Railroad interpretive trail; vault toilet, no potable water. Parking aprons ~11x42 ft fit a 23-ft rig. First-come, first-served. --Claude

10-site Malheur NF (Blue Mountain RD) campground on the Middle Fork John Day River off Co Rd 20, near Vinegar Hill with fishing and wildflowers; vault toilet, no potable water. Parking aprons ~18x40 ft. First-come, first-served. --Claude

6-site Malheur NF (Prairie City RD) campground on Lake Creek in Logan Valley off FR 924, near Strawberry Mountain Wilderness trailheads (just north of Lake Creek Youth Camp); vault toilet, no potable water. Drive-in on gravel forest road. First-come, first-served. --Claude

14-site Malheur NF (Blue Mountain RD) campground on Bear Creek in a high meadow off FR 16, direct road to Seneca; potable water, vault toilet, accessible sites. 6 pull-throughs, gravel pads to ~30 ft. First-come, first-served. --Claude

10-site Malheur NF (Prairie City RD) campground on Strawberry Creek at the edge of Strawberry Mountain Wilderness off FR 6001; hand-pump water, vault toilet. Access is ~9-10 mi gravel (Co Rd 60 + FR 6001); the last mile to the lake trailhead is narrow/steep/rough, but lower sites near the bridge fit rigs up to ~29 ft (firsthand review). First-come, first-served. --Claude

6-site Malheur NF (Prairie City RD) campground in the John Day River headwaters off Co Rd 62, with a stocked fishing pond and short loop trail; potable water, vault toilet, accessible sites, group picnic shelter. Drive-in gravel access. First-come, first-served. --Claude

BLM Prineville District string of ~9 small first-come, first-served campgrounds along the Lower Crooked Wild & Scenic River on Hwy 27 south of Prineville (Castle Rock, Stillwater, Lone Pine, Palisades, Chimney Rock, Cobble Rock, Post Pile, Poison Butte, Big Bend); ~97 total sites. Pinned to the main Chimney Rock Campground (16 sites, RVs to 32 ft, vault toilets, potable water, grey-water sumps). Open year-round, no reservations. --Claude

Small primitive Ochoco National Forest campground at a former gravel pit now filled with water (a locally popular swimming hole, sometimes stocked with trout), reached via FR 12 and FR 4274 spur (gravel). 3 established sites plus a large parking area, vault toilet, no potable water. 14-day limit; FCFS. --Claude

Ochoco National Forest campground among large ponderosa pine on the North Fork Crooked River at the mouth of Deep Creek; paved access most of the way. 15 well-spaced sites good for RVs and tents, vault/pit toilets, no potable water. 14-day limit; FCFS (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

Small primitive Ochoco National Forest campground in the Maury Mountains, ~5,200 ft, reached via Hwy 380 then gravel FR 16 / FR 16-350. 5 sites, vault toilet, no potable water; a short walk from Double Cabin Pond. Suited to tents and RVs; typically open May-September; FCFS. --Claude

Small Ochoco National Forest campground in the Maury Mountains, reached via Hwy 380 then gravel FR 16 (~5 mi in). 5 sites; noted as popular with trailer RVers for its easier road access and ample room to turn around or pull through. Vault toilet, no potable water; FCFS. --Claude

Ochoco National Forest campground on Mill Creek at the edge of the Mill Creek Wilderness, adjacent to the Twin Pillars trailhead; reached via Hwy 26 then FR 33 (Mill Creek Rd, gravel). 17 sites (incl. a group site); vault toilets, no potable water. Best for small-to-medium rigs given the intimate forest layout but drive-in and passable for a 23-ft RV. $50 group site; 14-day limit. --Claude

USFS Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (High Cascades RD), 10 sites on Mill Creek off FR 030 ~1 mi from OR-62 near Prospect. No hookups, no potable water, vault toilets, fire rings; no pull-throughs. Longest reported rig 23 ft (a 23-ft travel trailer fit per firsthand review). Scan-and-pay/on-site (cashless as of 7/2026). RV Life 0*/$ unrated (auto 7/2026). --Claude

BLM Coos Bay District, 10 sites on the Smith River just above Smith River Falls, ~26 mi E of Reedsport via Smith River Rd (paved then gravel). First-come, first-served; picnic tables, fire rings, accessible vault restrooms, boat launch, no drinking water. Open Memorial Day-Sept 30. RV Life 0*/$ unrated (auto 7/2026). --Claude

BLM Coos Bay District, 5 sites on the Smith River at the mouth of Vincent Creek, ~30 mi E of Reedsport via Smith River Rd. First-come, first-served; vault restroom, no drinking water, small swimming hole. Open Memorial Day-Sept 30. Satellite shows a riverside clearing with drive-in access. RV Life 0*/$ unrated (auto 7/2026). --Claude

Wallowa-Whitman NF (Whitman RD) small primitive campground below the Wild & Scenic Eagle Creek / Little Eagle Creek confluence, ~7.75 mi up mostly single-lane gravel FR 7735 from New Bridge. 7 tent/trailer sites, no hookups, seasonal drinking water; scan-and-pay/FCFS. No published max length; small forest sites. --Claude

BLM Burns District high-desert campground on Chickahominy Reservoir along US-20 ~32 mi W of Burns. 28 gravel-pad sites suitable for RVs, drinking water, vault toilets, fish-cleaning station and boat ramp; all sites first-come, first-served (no reservations). Popular trout fishery. --Claude

BLM Medford District primitive campground along the West Fork of Evans Creek NW of Rogue River, paved access. 11 paved primitive sites, picnic tables/grills, one pit toilet, no water/hookups; 14-day limit, FCFS. Multiple creek-access points with granite sand bars. In an OHV/trail area. --Claude

Umpqua NF (Diamond Lake RD) small campground on the Clearwater River near Clearwater Falls off Hwy 138. 9 sites (5 off Hwy 138, 4 upper via FR 4785), no hookups, no potable water; first-come, first-served (June-Oct). Vehicles 25 ft max due to winding approach. --Claude

USACE (John Day project) dispersed camping area: a level gravel flat on the Columbia River (Lake Umatilla) just west of John Day Dam, I-84 exit 109 at Rufus. Accommodates RVs up to ~45 ft, vault toilets, boat/kayak launch, no hookups; first-come first-served, 7-day limit. --Claude

Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Wild Rivers RD) primitive campground at a small historic mill pond, ~25 mi from Grants Pass via forest roads off Selma. 4 standard (non-walk-in) sites, no drinking water/no trash, toilet and accessible fishing platform; rec.gov Scan-and-Pay. Sites are small and RV space is limited - better suited to shorter rigs. --Claude

Fremont-Winema NF (Silver Lake RD) campground on Thompson Reservoir (~3 sq mi) under mature ponderosa pines, ~40 min south of Silver Lake via county road/FS Rd 27 (gravel). 19 tent/RV sites plus a group site, hand-pump water, 3 vault toilets, boat launch; max RV length 25 ft. First-come first-served. --Claude

Wallowa-Whitman NF (Whitman RD) campground ~3 mi NW of Sumpter on the Elkhorn Drive Scenic Byway; 7-8 sites among old-growth along McCully Fork creek, sites fit RVs up to 27 ft, vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups; FCFS. --Claude

Small Umatilla NF (North Fork John Day RD) camp on Bear Wallow Creek, ~11.5 mi E of Ukiah off Hwy 244. 8 gravel sites, vault toilets, no potable water/no garbage service; first-come, first-served. Open Memorial Day-mid Nov (snow closes access). --Claude

Umatilla NF camp in open ponderosa along the Wild & Scenic North Fork John Day River; from Ukiah S on Hwy 395 ~15 mi then E 7.7 mi on FR 55. 7 sites + group site, vault toilet, no potable water; first-come, first-served. Open Memorial Day-mid Nov. Historic Granite 9 mi S. --Claude

USFS (Wallowa-Whitman NF, Whitman RD) campground along Hwy 26 / Journey Through Time Scenic Byway ~9 mi W of Unity, beside Camp Creek. ~12 sites for tents and trailers (a couple large enough for 40-ft rigs), vault toilets, no potable water. Reservable on recreation.gov. Barrier-free trail links to Yellow Pine CG. --Claude

USFS (Wallowa-Whitman NF, Whitman RD) campground on Hwy 26 / Journey Through Time Scenic Byway ~10 mi W of Unity, along Camp Creek. Largest of the three byway campgrounds: 21 sites for tents and trailers (small/mid RVs, some sources cite up to ~30 ft), 5 accessible sites, vault toilets, no potable water. Reservable on recreation.gov. Barrier-free trail to Wetmore CG. --Claude

USFS (Wallowa-Whitman NF, Wallowa Mtns Office) rustic campground on the Wild & Scenic Imnaha River, off FR 39 (Hells Canyon Scenic Byway) via FR 3960 SE of Joseph. 10 tent/trailer drive-in sites, 3 accessible, vault toilet, no potable water (water at nearby Indian Crossing/Ollokot). Reservable on recreation.gov. Small rustic sites; check length for larger rigs. --Claude

USFS (Umatilla NF, Walla Walla RD) forested campground beside Target Meadow, ~20 mi E of Weston off Hwy 204 then FR 64 (gravel). ~17-22 sites among evergreens; most fit typical RVs and some are pull-through/drive-through best for longer rigs. Vault toilets, water (shut off ~Sep 30). Reservable on recreation.gov. --Claude

USFS (Umatilla NF, Walla Walla RD) riverside campground at the forks of the Umatilla River (N and S Fork confluence) E of Weston at end of FR 32. ~8-12 rustic sites in two clusters, drinking water, vault toilets; the upper cluster has a narrow/rough entry (non-trailer), the lower 'anyone' cluster takes trailers/small RVs. First-come, first-served. Best for smaller rigs. --Claude

Umatilla NF (Walla Walla Ranger District), ~20 mi E of Weston on Hwy 204 near Tollgate; paved highway access. About 14-18 standard nonelectric sites, max RV/trailer 25 ft, vault toilets, dump station on site, no hookups. Some sites reservable online, others first-come, first-served. Small pond/marsh beside the loop. --Claude

Rogue River-Siskiyou NF (Wild Rivers Ranger District), Briggs Valley SW of Grants Pass; centered on a historic meadow. About 19 standard nonelectric sites, max vehicle length ~24 ft, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (cashless scan-and-pay via Recreation.gov app). Access is via a narrow, winding, steep forest road (FR 2500/2512) - fine for a compact 23-ft rig but not large RVs. Separate Sam Brown Horse Camp is nearby. RV Life 0* (unrated)/$ (auto 7/2026). --Claude

BLM Northwest Oregon District (NOT Oregon Dept. of Forestry) on the Nestucca River National Back Country Byway along the Nestucca Wild & Scenic River, W of Willamina. About 10 sites plus a group shelter, paved parking pads, picnic tables/fire rings, two vault toilets, seasonal potable water, no hookups. Reservable online or first-come, first-served with on-site payment; season ~May-Sept, no cell reception in the drainage. --Claude

City of Coquille park at a former mill site on the Coquille River (off Hwy 42S, across from the DMV); open dry camping (no marked sites -- park on asphalt or grass), restrooms, boat ramp, fishing dock, on-site camp host. Reserve via Community Building (541-396-5131). --Claude

Jackson County park on the Applegate River (~1.75 mi frontage) near Ruch, 8 mi W of Jacksonville. 30 basic no-hookup sites (+1 group camp), flush restrooms with showers; sites take RVs/trailers though some are tight with narrow roads for larger rigs. First-come, first-served, no reservations, open ~Apr 10-Oct 5. --Claude

Malheur County park on a dead-end road ~15 min SW of Nyssa (on the Oregon Trail); 21 RV sites with electric (20/30/50-amp; only 2 full hookups) and water, restroom with showers, playground, ballfields, open year-round. No dump station on-site. --Claude

Operated by the Port of Tillamook Bay (a port district) beside the Tillamook municipal airport / Air Museum; basic spacious gravel sites for self-contained RVs and tents, mostly no hookups but potable water available, picnic tables and fire rings, no on-site dump station. Fits rigs to 50 ft; cash only. --Claude

Willow Creek Park District (a local special district) RV park on Willow Creek Reservoir/Lake, 0.5 mi up Willow Creek Rd off Hwy 207 at Heppner; 24 sites incl one host, pull-thrus 50-60 ft with water/electric, dump, boat launch, restrooms/showers; seasonal (spring-fall). Operated by a local park district -> reclassified private->local. --Claude

Wallowa-Whitman NF campground in the Grande Ronde River valley off Hwy 244, ~14 mi W of La Grande (I-84 exit 252). 22 wooded sites under ponderosa pines, vault toilets, no drinking water/hookups; reviewers report easy backing for larger rigs. Reservable on recreation.gov with some FCFS. Interpretive trail along the river across the road. --Claude
